title: Skeleton
summary: Loading placeholders are the system redaction: apply redacted(reason: .placeholder) to the real layout and its text and images are drawn as placeholder shapes. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: While content loads and its layout is known: build the view with sample data and redact it, so the placeholder has the size of the real content.
whenNotToUse: For a wait with no known layout, use a ProgressView. For a failure, use MonarchErrorState or MonarchInlineErrorRetry.

states.name: loading
states.description: Text and images are replaced by rounded placeholder shapes in the foreground colour.

states.name: loaded
states.description: Pass an empty reason set to show the content.

appearance: System placeholder shapes, which take the foreground colour of the redacted views, so they follow the theme's text colours in every theme. They do not animate.
platformNotes: The parity map lists a shimmer modifier beside the redaction. No shimmer is shipped: a modifier would be a Swift type, which a native-adoption entry does not have, and the system placeholder is static, so there is nothing to stop under Reduce Motion. Android builds MonarchSkeleton and the web Skeleton shimmers; if the same is wanted here it is a separate build entry. The web shape, width and height props have no equivalent, because the placeholder takes the shape of the real views.
accessibility: System behaviour: redacted text is still read by VoiceOver as its sample content. Group the redacted region as one element with accessibilityElement(children: .ignore) and give it a label such as "Loading contact".
The placeholder does not move, so Reduce Motion needs no handling.
edgeCases: Monarch components draw their text and icons with Text and Image, so they redact with the rest of the layout.
Backgrounds, borders and custom shapes are not redacted.
unredacted() keeps one part readable while the rest loads.

examples.title: Shapes
examples.template:
HStack(spacing: 8) {
    Circle()
        .fill(theme.colors.bgMuted)
        .frame(width: {{shapes.0.width}} * 16, height: {{shapes.0.height}} * 16)
    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: theme.radius.md)
        .fill(theme.colors.bgMuted)
        .frame(width: {{shapes.1.width}} * 16, height: 16)
    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: theme.radius.md)
        .fill(theme.colors.bgMuted)
        .frame(width: {{shapes.2.width}} * 16, height: {{shapes.2.height}} * 16)
}
.accessibilityHidden(true)
examples.code:
HStack(spacing: 8) {
    Circle()
        .fill(theme.colors.bgMuted)
        .frame(width: 2.5 * 16, height: 2.5 * 16)
    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: theme.radius.md)
        .fill(theme.colors.bgMuted)
        .frame(width: 12 * 16, height: 16)
    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: theme.radius.md)
        .fill(theme.colors.bgMuted)
        .frame(width: 8 * 16, height: 2 * 16)
}
.accessibilityHidden(true)

parityExceptions.reason: Decision: web-only, the platform convention applies. There is no Monarch skeleton view on iOS, so the circle, text and rect shapes are drawn directly with bgMuted fills.
